svg.aria-label: Overall architecture of Runtime X-Ray: an orchestrator launches a Java virtual machine observed by three tools, which write their measurements to disk; the orchestrator reads them back and assembles a self-contained page
svg.title: Runtime X-Ray — overall architecture
svg.text: The jar observes nothing itself: it launches the application, lets three tools measure, then reads back what they wrote.
NO NETWORK ACCESS WHILE IT RUNS
instruments nothing, profiles nothing — no dependency outside the Java Development Kit
All three measure the SAME run.
write their outputs, each in its own format
the only durable thing: everything else is derived from it
read back and assembled — by the same jar
one file to open, no external resource,
readable on a machine with nothing installed
Three tools, three questions, and not one of
them answers all three: it is their union that
answers, and the orchestrator only lays it out.
Everything that is read — the page, the facts,
the diagnostic — is derived from runs/.
Deleting the page loses nothing; deleting
The network appears once, outside the zone,
and at install time. While the application
